name: Battery energy storage (BESS)
summary: Utility-scale lithium-ion (LFP) BESS priced per MWh of energy capacity, default 4-hour duration. The DC block (cells, racks, containers) is 50–65% of cost and has fallen sharply since 2023, so 2023-dollar engineering estimates (EIA/S&L ≈ $414k/MWh EPC) now sit at the top of the range while 2025 market ranges (Lazard LCOS v10 ≈ $140–365k/MWh installed) define the middle. Data quality: good, but prices are moving fast and are tariff-sensitive — verify against current quotes.

typicalSize.method: Mid = Lazard utility-scale standalone reference 100 MW / 400 MWh (e2); EIA reference 150 MW / 600 MWh (e1). Low 20 MWh ≈ 5 MW distribution-connected project; high 1,200 MWh ≈ 300 MW / 4 h large ISO project.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: e1 estimated land requirement 6 acres for 600 MWh = 100 MWh/acre incl. substation. Range ±40–50% for fire-code spacing (NFPA 855 / AHJ), setbacks and container density.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Unstaffed facility; a few gravel spaces at the control building only.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard cost = EPC/turnkey installed price per MWh (4-hr). e2 Lazard LCOS v10 (2025): total initial installed cost $56–146M for 100 MW/400 MWh = $140k–365k/MWh, midpoint $253k (DC block + PCS + EPC; excludes interconnection, development). e3 DOE/NREL 2025Q1: PV+ESS minus PV-only MMP = $0.69/Wdc × 100 MWdc / 240 MWh = $288k/MWh (2024$, incl. developer margin; × 0.90 ≈ $259k hard). e1 EIA/S&L EPC $248.1M / 600 MWh = $414k/MWh in 2023$ (pre-2024 cell-price decline; includes $10.5M substation). Mid = average of the two current points ($253k, $259k) ≈ $256k, nudged up to $265k for US tariff exposure on Chinese cells. Low = Lazard low ($140k) rounded to $150k; high = EIA 2023 EPC ($414k → $415k) as an upper bound representing small/complex or domestic-content projects. Evidence years 2023–2025 (EIA is >1 yr older; used only for the high bound).

scope.notes: Turnkey EPC: battery containers/enclosures, PCS/inverters, MV transformers, collection cabling, foundations, SCADA/EMS, on-site project substation, civil work, EPC indirects/fee/contingency. Excludes land, interconnection line and network upgrades, developer soft costs, augmentation and financing.

systemSplit.method: From EIA/S&L Case 19 EPC components (total $248.144M): 48 = BESS unit supply 151.7 + 60% of BESS installation (8.672); BOP equipment supply 36.857 (inverters, MV transformers, cabling, foundations, SCADA per note 2) split 26 = 85%, 03 = 10%, 25 = 5%; remaining installation split 31 = 25%, 32 = 15%; 33 = main power transformer & substation 10.5; 01 = indirects 17.345 + EPC fee 11.254 + EPC contingency 11.816. The BOP and installation sub-splits are assumptions (verify). Note that with 2025 cell prices the 48 share is likely lower (~0.55) than this 2023 estimate.

lineItems.name: DC block — LFP cells, racks, containers, BMS, HVAC/fire suppression

cost.method: e2 Lazard 'Initial Capital Cost—DC' $107–232/kWh for utility-scale standalone 100 MW/400 MWh; mid = midpoint rounded.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out of the baseline; most tariff-sensitive line.

lineItems.name: Power conversion system (inverters/PCS), per kW at 4-hr duration

cost.method: e2 Lazard 'Initial Capital Cost—AC' $25–67/kW (100 MW/400 MWh); qty 250 kW per MWh = 4-hour duration.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out. Shorter-duration (2-h) systems need 500 kW per MWh.

cost.method: e2 Lazard 'EPC Costs' $28–116/kWh (100 MW/400 MWh); mid = midpoint.

lineItems.name: Project substation & main power transformer

cost.method: e1 'Main Power Transformer & Substation' $10.5M for 150 MW. Low for small distribution-connected projects; high for 345 kV+ class.

lineItems.notes: Inside the baseline for transmission-connected projects.

lineItems.name: Generator tie / transmission line to POI

cost.method: e1 transmission line $2,412,000/mile ÷ 5,280 = $457/LF; default 1 mile. Range ±35% assumed.

lineItems.notes: Owner's interconnection cost, outside the property line.

lineItems.name: Capacity augmentation reserve (future cells to hold rated MWh)

cost.method: Lazard excludes augmentation from capital cost (e2); EIA notes ~1.5% average annual degradation (e1). Allowance ≈ 10–20% of DC block cost ($107–232k) for first augmentation; present-valued placeholder. Verify with the LTSA/warranty structure.

lineItems.notes: Often capitalized later; include only if the budget must carry it.

pctOfHard.method: e1 owner's services = 4% of EPC; total owner's costs (services, land, 1-mile interconnection, contingency) $13.522M = 5.4% of EPC → low. Mid 8% / high 12% add developer fees, interconnection studies, financing fees and fire-code/AHJ studies typical of merchant or smaller projects. | Second pass (2026-10-24, main session): Reduced 2 points to remove developer fees and financing fees added in the mid/high. The engine adds impact & tap fees, the developer fee and construction financing as their own lines (docs/BUDGET_ENGINE.md §5), so this bucket must exclude them.

softCosts.notes: Network upgrades and gen-tie are separate line items.

design.method: Containerized, repetitive design; main design risks are fire-code layout and geotech.

hard.method: e1 EPC contingency 5% of EPC costs used as mid; high for tariff/supply-chain exposure.

soft.method: e1 owner's contingency 5% of owner's costs.

perPrimaryUnit.method: All-in hard + soft (excl. land): low end = Lazard low $140k/MWh; high end = EIA 2023 total capital cost $436/kWh plus margin for small or 2-hour systems (higher $/MWh because PCS is spread over fewer MWh).

source.title: Capital Cost and Performance Characteristic Estimates for Utility Scale Electric Power Generating Technologies (Sargent & Lundy for EIA), Case 19 Battery Energy Storage System, 150 MW | 600 MWh
source.publisher: U.S. Energy Information Administration / Sargent & Lundy

evidence.quote: Table 19-1 — Case 19 Capital Cost Estimate (2023 $): BESS Unit Supply $151,700,000 ... EPC Subtotal $248,144,000 ... Total Capital Cost $261,666,000; $/kW net 1,744; $/kWh 436; Estimated Land Requirement 6 acres.
evidence.scopeNotes: Value = EPC subtotal / 600 MWh. Includes MPT & substation ($10.5M), EPC fee 5% and contingency 5%. Owner's costs (services 4%, land, interconnection, contingency) excluded. Priced before the 2024–2025 LFP cell price drop.

source.title: Lazard's Levelized Cost of Energy+ (June 2025) — Levelized Cost of Storage Analysis, Version 10.0, key assumptions (Utility-Scale Standalone 100 MW / 400 MWh)

evidence.quote: Utility-Scale Standalone (100 MW/400 MWh): Initial Capital Cost—DC $107 – $232 /kWh; Initial Capital Cost—AC $25 – $67 /kW; EPC Costs $28 – $116 /kWh; Total Initial Installed Cost $56 – $146 M $.
evidence.scopeNotes: Capital costs include storage module, BOS, power conversion equipment and EPC; excludes augmentation, interconnection/network upgrades and development costs. Range = $56M/400 MWh to $146M/400 MWh.

source.title: Solar Photovoltaic System Cost Benchmarks (2025Q1 benchmarks)
source.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Solar Energy Technologies Office (NREL modeling)

evidence.quote: Representative UPV system 100 MWdc; Table 1 PV + ESS (240 MWh): MMP $1.81/Wdc; Table 2 PV-only: MMP $1.12/Wdc. All dollar values are inflation-adjusted to 2024 U.S. dollars.
evidence.scopeNotes: Derived: ($1.81 − $1.12)/Wdc × 100 MWdc = $69M for 240 MWh = $287.5k/MWh. Co-located (shares some BOS), modeled market price incl. developer overhead/profit.

openQuestions: NREL ATB / 'Cost Projections for Utility-Scale Battery Storage: 2025 Update' and BNEF US turnkey survey figures could not be retrieved (nrel.gov unreachable; BNEF coverage 403). Add them.
Ember (Oct 2025) puts a full grid-connected 4-h system outside China/US at ~$125/kWh — the US premium (tariffs, FEOC rules) should be quantified.
Fire-code (NFPA 855) spacing and large-scale fire testing costs vary by AHJ.
Split between energy-related ($/kWh) and power-related ($/kW) costs matters for 2-h vs 8-h systems; engine assumes 4-h.
